extraction.name: CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images
extraction.description: A dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed images used to train open diffusion models
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We focus on locating high-resolution Creative-Commons images that have open licenses. We began with the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files, as well as Flickr IDs linking to the original data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Web Scraping, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: CC images rarely have the alt-text captions necessary to train a high-quality T2I model.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: We use a pre-trained BLIP-2 model to produce high-quality, synthetic captions for a set of curated, open licensed CC images.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We center-cropped and resized all of the images to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels for captioning.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We used a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model for synthesizing CommonCatalog’s captions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Our models, data, and code are released at https://github.com/mosaicml/diffusion/blob/main/assets/common-canvas.md.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Our work indicates that it is possible to efficiently produce a high-quality T2I model by training only on Creative-Commons-licensed data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Our model underperformed in several categories, including faces, general photography, and paintings.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Our model has limitations, such as underperforming in certain categories and potentially generating problematic content with adversarial prompts.
